counterfactual_missing_items: No additional cutaneous or mucosal lesions were present
decisive_items: Revealed epidermal erosion with suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
response.rationale: R2 is strongly supported by suprabasal acantholysis, intercellular IgG/C3 deposition, and anti-desmoglein 3-predominant autoantibodies, which are diagnostic of pemphigus vulgaris. R1 lacks any evidence of an associated neoplasm; Crohn disease is not a paraneoplastic trigger, and the absence of mucosal lesions argues against paraneoplastic pemphigus.

rejected.why: No underlying malignancy is present; Crohn disease is not a paraneoplastic neoplasm, and the histopathologic and serologic findings are characteristic of pemphigus vulgaris rather than paraneoplastic pemphigus.
